title: Tennis and jazz: serves and age
summary: He compares tennis rhythm to jazz and talks about Rosewall, Tanner and watching matches.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Is there any similarity between Jazz and Tennis?

Uh, there must be! I never thought of this. I know that there is an awful lot of rhythm connected with tennis. I can tell by watching the guy's serve whether he has the ability to be a good tennis player or not.

Now, there is a guy from South Africa, his name is Kevin Curran. You ever heard of him? He's got a real fast-draw serve. He's like Roscoe Tanner, in a way. And you know, when Roscoe Tanner lost his serve... His serve disappeared, you know, he started hitting that net instead of putting them over and making forty aces in a row, like he used to. His rating went [PLUMMETING SOUND]. You don't hear anybody talk about Roscoe Tanner any more. He used to serve the ball 145 miles an hour. That's fast. That'll take your eye out. But he didn't have anything else. He was just fair.

But you take a guy like Rosewall. Now, Rosewall has got an easy serve, he puts it right where he wants to put it, with just enough speed n it and just enough mageu(?) that he knows what's going to happen on the return. Unless he is playing a guy like Laver, who they've played ever since they were ten years old... But he knows how to

trick... And the only reason why Connors beat him in Salt Lake City is because of the difference in age and the power. Because as far as the smarts is concerned, Connors was still getting the smarts. Rosewall already had 'em. But he's too old. No way...

You know, your eyes go. That's one of the most important things in tennis. People don't realize, if your eyes are not absolutely perfect, you're through. Because if you have to get up against a guy who's got a fast serve, you've got to be able to see that ball. Man, you can't just depend on anticipation.

Did you ever go to the tennis matches? Where do you sit? Do you sit in the middle and turn your head this way, or do you sit at the end and watch the strategy? That's the way to watch a tennis match. Sit up about halfway, and watch what the guy is doing.
Go with Paul Whisenant(?) sometime. He knows.
